dossier.public_summary: A bright secondary dip at half an orbit and a large brightness swing outside the dips both point to a stellar companion, not a planet. The dip also changes depth from sector to sector and sits exactly at the star's spin period, matching an active eclipsing binary on the target.

reasons.why: Deep second eclipse at half phase at 18% of primary depth, well above noise and comparable to brightening, is stellar eclipsing binary signature; hot planet would be at ppm.
reasons.value: snr 11.02 phase 0.4885 depth_ppm 1244 depth_over_dip 0.1759 snr_at_half 10.15 best_brightening_snr 43.57

reasons.why: Large out-of-eclipse modulation at the same period as the dip indicates ellipsoidal/beaming from a close binary, not a planet.
Signal period is exactly the stellar rotation period with large spot amplitude, favouring variability/binary as the source over a stable planet.

Depth changes by factor ~4 both across and within the same pipeline, far beyond calibration, with duration-density mismatch; centroid on_target but xgboost planet_rank 0.1 and similar objects are mostly not a planet.
